_why: Ground truth for the fingerprint: would a stranger say these two came from
one tool, or from two different studios?
JUDGED FROM THE WHOLE PAGE, scrolled top to bottom, not from the first
viewport. That changed on 2026-09-08 and it is a change of definition rather
than of method. Every verdict before it was read off a fold screenshot, and a
fold cannot see an axis that lives below it: page architecture rendered
`ledger` byte-identical to `stacked` above the fold, so its binding claim
could not have passed however good the axis was. Section edges and most of
the signature device are down there too. An instrument that only looks at one
screen can only ever validate first-screen axes.
The pictures are artifacts/contact-sheet/<slug>-page.png, written by
tools/contact_sheet.py alongside pages.html. They are not committed: ten
megabytes a run on a directory rewritten every time the corpus is re-decided,
in a repository that has already had a push fail on size. The full-size
sheets have never been committed for the same reason, and the tool
regenerates all of it deterministically.
Judged BLIND, with no axis values in view. The first version of this file was
contaminated — four of four 'different' verdicts were justified in the
vector's own vocabulary — so every `why` below describes what is on the
screen. If a verdict cannot be written that way it is not a judgement about
the picture.
THE RESOLVING RULES, re-checked against the new definition rather than
carried over on assumption:
COLOUR AND SUBJECT still do not make a different site on their own. Two pages
identical down their length in different accents are one tool painted twice,
and whoever is in the photograph is not a design decision. But the check
found one thing the fold hid: a ground that ALTERNATES down the page is not
colour, it is arrangement — a stack of slabs against an even field reads as a
different page even when both are the same hue. Colour is discounted where it
is paint and counted where it is structure, and the test is whether it
changes with position on the page.
TYPE SETTING still does not make a different site on its own — size, case,
letter-spacing. The words differ between any two businesses so the lettering
always differs; what a stranger recognises is the arrangement. It counts when
it moves the type somewhere else or changes what shares the screen with it.
AND NEWLY IN SCOPE, because the fold could not see it: the RHYTHM of the
bands down the page, the MEASURE the text is set to, and whether the bands
are separated by rules, by ground changes, or by whitespace alone. These are
arrangement and they count.

AND A SIGNATURE DEVICE counts when it changes the page's proportions, on the same test the type-setting rule uses. A full screen of display quotation does; a hairline of running facts, a row of stamps or a strip of pictures does not, on its own. Added 2026-09-08 when the device became an axis, and stated before the pairs it decides were looked at.

_judged_against: Whole-page renderings of the corpus as of the signature device landing — distance ruler d2f37ed7, gate rule 95f4d93e — from artifacts/contact-sheet/pages.html.
_held_out: One verdict in three, chosen by a hash of the two slugs so that nobody picks which evidence survives. A held-out verdict is never used to choose a rule or a weighting, only to score one afterwards, and it is never re-judged — when the page under it changes it is retired with a reason and the set gets smaller. It starts here, so it says nothing about the rule this commit lands: the first rule it can honestly score is the next one.
_retired: A retired verdict is scored by nothing and re-judged by nobody. Retiring is what happens to a held-out pair when the page under it changes, and to any pair whose subject turns out not to be judgeable — the set shrinks, which is the honest cost of the number meaning anything.
